articleTitle: A review of routing protocols for underwater wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Underwater wireless sensor networks (UWSNs) are a prominent research topic in academia and industry, with a wide range of underwater applications including ocean monitoring, seismic monitoring, environmental monitoring, and seabed exploration. However, UWSNs face a number of restrictions and obstacles, including high ocean interference and noise, long propagation times, narrow bandwidth, changeable network architecture, and sensor's battery life. One of the solutions to these problems is to build efficient routing protocols. A routing protocol can move data from a source node to a destination node in the network efficiently. A review of underwater routing protocols for UWSNs is presented in this paper. Existing underwater routing protocols are categorized into three categories: energy-based, data-based, and geographic information-based protocols. Recent underwater routing protocols are discussed in depth, by presenting their benefits, drawbacks and performance. In addition, We discuss challenges and future directions of underwater routing protocols, which can assist researchers interested to explore further this important research topic.

articleTitle: An improved hyperbolic tangent power rate sliding mode operating islanded AC smartgrid based master-slave
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: This paper presents an amalgamation between power rate sliding mode (PRSMC) and hyperbolic tangent (Tanh) sliding mode control to enhance the active and reactive power sharing between two parallel inverters in AC microgrid-based master-slave topology. The proposed control scheme comprises the outer control loop (master unit) that is based on a Proportional Integral (PI) controller and the inner control loop (slave unit) that is based on the proposed (PRTanh) sliding mode controller. Moreover, the suggested method works toward tackling the stability and robustness issues in the conventional sliding mode control. The microgrid under study comprises two parallel 3-level diode clamped inverters operated in islanded mode and connected to a common load through the Point of Common Coupling (PCC). Simulation results are carried out utilizing MATLAB/Simulink, where the suggested controller is compared to other controllers to prove its reliability, robustness, and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Intelligent system for governing risks in smart cities applications
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: This paper presents an intelligent system to manage risks in smart cities. This system is based on mining social media big perceptions by using natural language processing in identifying and assessing risks. It will help the authority of smart cities in managing risks processes. In addition, a related survey for the most relevant research articles in the area of risk management in smart cities is included. Besides, we provide a framework to the proposed system and describe it mathematically as well as explicit mathematical expressions such as identifying risks in tweets are driven. Moreover, a real data is collected from profiles of London citizens on Twitter, and risk analysis and assessment are performed. Furthermore, performance measures are included to show the validity of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Deep learning-based Alzheimer's disease prediction for smart health system
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Smart Health (s-Health) is used in improving healthcare by providing many services such as patient monitoring and early diagnosis of diseases. In this context, Alzheimer's disease (AD) begins years before the first clinical symptoms emerge. Early diagnosis is essential to ensure adequate patient care. This work aims to propose a new method to predict this disease. Our method is based on deep learning which combines the techniques of data augmentation, the pretrained “VGG-16” model and transfer learning. In order to evaluate the performance of our method, we conducted a series of experiments on Kaggle Alzheimer's dataset. The proposed solution offers an accuracy rate of 91.75%.

articleTitle: Continual learning using EfficientNet and data generation for remote sensing image classification
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: In the image classification field, deep learning showed great achievements such as high-resolution image classification and segmentation. Due to the adoption of static training approaches, modern deep learning algorithms suffer from the long training time and the large amount of data required for training. Traditional end-to-end deep learning methods are unable to make incremental learning since it needs to acquire new knowledge without losing previously learned knowledge. In order to solve the forgetting issue, continual learning has lately been employed. It includes two main steps: the continuous update and the optimization of the learning model for learning knowledge progressively. In this paper, we proposed a modern continual learning approach for the classification of high-resolution remote sensing image scenes based on previously observed data auto-generation sub-networks. Scene classification is an important challenge for Remote Sensing applications. It is a difficult task, particularly for huge datasets. The suggested neural network architecture includes two trainable sub-networks. For the new task acquisition, the modification of weights is achieved in the first module with the reduction of discrimination between land-cover classes error. Simultaneously, the responsibility of the second module is learning the task data reproduction by understanding the new task dataset's latent data structure. Experiments are carried out on the Merced dataset. In our experiment we get an overall accuracy of 97%. The results confirmed the suggested model's strength.

articleTitle: Classification of lung sounds using Deep Neural Network (DNN) for accurate and robust diagnosis of lung diseases
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: The respiratory system can malfunction due to various diseases and abnormalities. Several diagnostic approaches have been developed over the years. Among them, auscultation of the respiratory system performed using a stethoscope is the most common approach used due to its simplicity and affordability. However, such an approach is subjective and depends on the physician's hearing acuity. Nevertheless, since the respiratory system generates a mixture of sounds originating from different locations, it is hard to differentiate between the auscultations by only relying on the hearing skills. The primary objective of this paper is to investigate different classification models and strategies to differentiate breathing sound anomalies for automated diagnosis with the help of an AI algorithm (supervised learned network) that extracts sound features and analyzes them to perform quadric-categorical classification (Normal, Crackles, Wheezes, Crackles and Wheezes). Based on the available literature, two most suitable approaches were investigated. Artificial Neural Network (ANN) with statistical features and Convolution Neural Network (CNN) with time-frequency spectrum. The performance of both methods was assessed using readily available single channel pulmonary sounds. After Training both neural networks on 280 different pulmonary sounds, results show that classifying using time-frequency analysis is much reliable when it comes to analyzing lung auscultation with an accuracy of 100%, while on another hand the statistical approach shows an accuracy of 95% for the same dataset examined. This is mainly because of its sensitivity to any changes in the spatial features and its capability to store information thus, classify sounds accurately.

articleTitle: Detecting distributed DoS attacks in autonomous vehicles external environment using machine learning techniques
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: The use of autonomous vehicles rapidly growing, especially in smart cities. Autonomous vehicles exchange information with an external network through wireless communication, and hence security and privacy challenges become a major challenge for all user of autonomous vehicles. Attackers try to exploit the vulnerabilities in the wireless network that connect autonomous vehicles these by performing different types of attacks such as denial of service attack (DDOS) and injection attacks. To mitigate the catastrophic effect of these attacks, intrusion detection process is a must. In this paper, A novel intrusion-detection method is proposed to detect distributed denial of service attack (DDOS) in the wireless network of autonomous vehicles. In this method, the wireless network intrusion detection system (WNIDS) is applied on “CICDDoS2019” dataset for training and testing our model. First the dataset is cleaned and the most important features are selected using recursive feature elimination method which decrease the number of features to only 8 features. The reduced dataset is tested by two machine learning classifiers (Random Forest (RF) and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)). The evaluation results showed that both RF and SGD classifiers can be used to detect DDOS attack with an accuracy of 99% using only 8 features, which were selected using the proposed feature selection method. Relying only on 8 features only make the proposed method to be applicable to any IoT application such as internet of autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Analyzing domestic energy behavior with a multi-dimensional appliance-level dataset
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Data, in its purest nature, has an authority on the systems it accompanies by feeding an accurate representation of the observed reality. In energy efficiency, the underlying motivation for big data efforts revolves around the intrinsic need to understand end-user electric energy consumption and means to improve it. Hence, developing a rich, detailed, and realistic power consumption dataset entails a deliberate process of preparing the data collection environment, configuring proper Internet of Energy (IoE) sensors and managing the collected data. In this work, a novel power consumption dataset is presented in efforts to improve the state-of-the-art of energy efficiency research in buildings. The dataset is also accompanied by a two-dimensional (2D) counterpart produced using Gramian Angular Fields (GAF) that creates pictorial summaries from one-dimensional (1D) data. Data acquisition is carried out using the ODROIDXU4 edge computing hub, Home Assistant software, and a collection of smart plugs and sensors. A notable use case is presented to signify the merits of the data and its analysis tools to achieve computationally efficient classification.

articleTitle: Intelligent machine learning based model for customer churn prediction in business sectors
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: In recent times, customer churn prediction (CCP) remains a hot research topic among data analysts and business people. The proper design of CCP models helps to alleviate the financial loss of the company by preventing the customers from leaving the product or services. This study introduces a new intelligent machine learning-based model for customer churn prediction in business sectors. The proposed model is a hybrid of bacterial foraging optimization algorithm with kernel extreme learning machine (BFOA-KELM). The major focus of the BFOA-KELM technique is to identify the presence of customer churns or not in the business sector. The proposed BFOA-KELM method involves the design of effective KELM classification method, which categorizes the input customer data as to 2 class labels such as churn and non-churn. With an intention of enhancing the customer churn classification outcomes, the BFOA is applied to it and consequently it leads to enhanced outcomes. In order to exhibit the improved performance of the BFOA-KELM method, a set of simulations were carried out and the outcomes are investigated in various aspects. The comprehensive comparison study reported the enhanced outcomes of the BFOA-KELM model compared to its existing models.

articleTitle: Extended state observer-based neural networks with super-twisting sliding mode control feedback stabilizer
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: This paper presents a new intelligent control scheme consisting of a super-twisting second-order sliding mode control along with a neural network based extended state observer. Implementing the neural network with the extended state observer is intended to expand the operational range of the observer, avoiding the need to tune the observer whenever subjected to a new set of control challenges. Additionally, the high order of the sliding mode provides robust performance that improves the capability of the control scheme. The Bayesian regularization training function is used to train the neural network, where this technique has the potential capability of capturing nonlinear relationships to provide a robust model insensitive to noise. The performance of the proposed approach is compared to the conventional version of the observer, and various case studies were considered to demonstrate the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Sleep Apnea detecting based on ECG and EEG signals using Discrete Wavelet Transform and Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Sleep apnea is a severe sleep disorder that happens when breathing stops and starts during slumber. If it goes untreated, it can cause serious health problems. In recent years, Sleep Apnea (SA) has been diagnosed using either Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals that refer the heart health or Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals that refer to brain health. This research aims to build an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) classification model to determine sleep disorders using ECG and EEG signals. Features Delta sub-band waves are extracted and processed using a multilayer perceptron (MLP) with two different topologies; hidden layers are the same. The results show that using ECG and EEG signals to classify sleep apnea achieves high accuracy of 99.97% compared to other recent related work. We anticipate our assay to be a starting point for reliable wearable diagnostic devices to control equipment that can help patients with sleep apnea avoid respiratory distress episodes.

articleTitle: Performance of OpenFlow-based SDN on IoT network
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Every day we are getting more and more connected devices to our connected network knotweed Internet of Things (IoT) so it requires new methods to secure the network and the data! So in our research to make the connected network we did enlarge the search to the Software-defined Network (SDN) is a way that permit the network is configurable and a centralized management the thing that lead to a dynamic management to the network

articleTitle: Epileptic Seizure Detection using short time Fourier transform and Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: The progress of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been the most remarkable in the 21st Century. However, how far AI must have gone, it works in healthcare remains a big challenge for great minds across the globe. Epilepsy is a neurological disorder that occurs in a human being at any stage in life. Thus, frequent to rare seizures are faced by an individual having epilepsy and sometimes lead to death. The electroencephalogram (EEG) signals help diagnose this ailment. However, often long EEG signal takes a day or more even for trained neurologists to detect this disorder and may even lead to human errors. Thus, it becomes imperative to develop a robust and computationally efficient system that can help detect this ailment without causing delays and human error. This paper aims to extract the time-frequency plane from time domain signals using Short-time Fourier transform (STFT) and develop a neural network model using CNN to classify seizures. This paper has achieved the highest classification accuracy of 100% for some of the experiments and 95-99% accuracy for a few of them, thus helping better classify health and seizures with less computation required.

articleTitle: Viola-Jones and the speeded-up robust transformation model for multiple face detection and recognition in the images
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Face detection and recognition have garnered considerable interest due to their immense potential in various applications (criminal justice system, security, surveillance, image database investigation, human-computer interactions, innovative card application, multimedia, civilian applications, and video indexing). Multiple Face Detection and Recognition in an Image was performed using a hybrid model of optimized Viola-Jones and the Speeded-Up Robust transformation (SURF) approach. Viola-Jones was used to detect all faces inside a picture. Viola-Jones algorithm has been used to Improvement features classification in the learning part. Firstly, we use the threshold modulation function to identify the different parts of the human face while some non-facial regions are deleted. Increase AdaBoost performance by utilizing a new threshold value (3) for identifying all the faces in the image instead of the standard value threshold (4). The features were extracted using the SURF technique. The (CMU-MIT) data set devided into 70 percent training and 30 percent testing sets. The Squared Euclidean Distance measures has been used to calculate the accuracy recognition rate. The principal findings indicated that the suggested system had a recognition rate of 98.95% and that the face detection stage was 100% accurate.

articleTitle: Intelligent model for lung cancer detection using fusion analysis in CT images
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: One of the leading causes of death worldwide, lung cancer is the habitual use of tobacco products. Human life is threatened by unchecked cell development in the lung tissue. The use of CAD methods, namely correct demonstration, allows for early detection of lung cancer. An enhanced kind of artificial neural network, deep learning (DL) techniques use multiple layers to process their input, produce high-order characteristics, and finally output a projected value. The convolutional neural network (CNN) is one kind of deep learning that has found extensive use in computer vision applications. Rapid and accurate illness diagnosis became more challenging for radiologists as the volume of CT scan pictures increased. Hence, DL approaches were applied for the early identification of lung cancer as the need for CAD for lung cancer diagnosis increased. To train and test CAD, we examined 15,000 images of histopathology slides of adenocarcinomas, lung squamous cell carcinoma, and three kinds of benign lung tissue that were made accessible to the public. Extracting features from images required the use of multi-scale processing. The research was completed by comparing seven different CNN models for lung cancer classification: To ensure optimal performance, all pre-trained models are giggly to optimize parameters. With this approach, you can count on a minimal classification error of 0.090 and overall accuracy of 98.67 percent.

articleTitle: Tracking control of a rotary flexible joint robot: a comparative study
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Conventional PID controller is very common for industrial processes because of their simplicity and acceptable performance. However, the PID controller cannot effectively manage the large disturbances and has limitations of its own. This study aims to develop sophisticated controllers for the Rotary flexible joint, such as Fuzzy Logic Controllers (FLC) and Internal Model Controllers (IMC). The mathematical modeling of the Rotary Flexible Joint (RFJ) is theoretically investigated and developed in MATLAB and SIMULINK to design a Fuzzy logic-based IMC controller. Gaussian membership functions and the Mamdani method were used to design the FLC. Furthermore, an IMC controller is also desigend for the same model. In this paper, the performance of the PID, FLC, and IMC was compared through simulations. The objective was to keep track of a desired position angle and minimize the vibration of the joint. Simulation results show that the IMC controller performs better than the other two controllers since it successfully manages the disturbances and tracks the set point efficiently.

articleTitle: Arabic sign language recognition algorithm based on deep learning for smart cities
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: The deaf community relies on sign language as a primary means of communication. Automatic finger spelling recognition transcribes sign language into text. Such recognition will facilitate communication between deaf-mutes and ordinary citizens. The present work proposes a new method for static Arabic sign language recognition. Our method is based on the deep learning Alexnet model and the categorical cross-entropy loss function. It recognizes 32 classes of alphabets. The advantages of our method have been demonstrated experimentally on ArSL2018 dataset. The experiments show that our method offers an average F-measure of 97.38%.

articleTitle: Edge detection with multi-scale representation and refined Network
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Edge detection is a representation of boundaries between objects and regions in an image. Due to the variations of types, scales, intensities as well as background, the detection of these boundaries represents a challenge for different computer vision algorithms. The exploitation of multi-scale representation using various deep learning backbones make edge detection more realistic. However, edge detection is still not effective in terms of erroneous detection in some scenarios and the quality of detected edges. In this paper, we attempted to overcome these challenges using a high-resolution and refined network by fusing the output of different scales of the network and the output of the first layers. The proposed network used horizontal and vertical blocks, while the horizontal block (HB) contains a set of convolution layers and the vertical block (VB) represent the different scale of the image using convolution and pooling layers. The output of each scale in VR is combined with the corresponding layer in HB. Then, we used an affined batch normalization layer as an erosion operation for the homogeneous region in the image before fusing these outputs for the final edge detection results. The proposed method is evaluated using the most challenging datasets including BSDS500, NYUD, and Multicue. The obtained results outperform the designed edge detection networks in terms of performance metrics and quality of output images.

articleTitle: The preference ranking of gold nanoparticle synthesis methods using a multi-criteria decision-making model
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: In this technology-advancing world, nanotechnology is one of the fast-developing fields. Nanoparticles, gold nanoparticles (AuNPs), in particular, have a huge impact on science starting from the medical area and emphasizing the engineering part. Due to their enormous characteristics, including optical, electrical, physical, chemical, and surface plasmon resonance, gold nanoparticles have been widely examined and are known to have significant medical uses. According to their importance, the synthesis of gold nanoparticles is crucial to understand and because of numerous drawbacks found in the methods of production, it is still difficult to choose an appropriate, effective, cost-efficient, and eco-friendly synthesis method to use. Therefore, this study aims at analyzing and select the synthesis methods of AuNPs. Different synthesis methods were chosen in this study namely, biological, sonochemical, ɣ-irradiation, the brust-Schiffrin, photochemical, seeding growth, electrochemical, lithography, turkevich, chemical, and physicochemical. These techniques were ranked depending on the weight assigned to the selected criteria some of which include the toxicity effect, the manufacturing cost, the processing time, temperature-dependency, pH-dependency, radiation-dependency, size and purity of the final product, and many more by applying a multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) method; fuzzy Preference Ranking Organization Method for Enrichment Evaluations (fuzzy PROMETHEE). Biological synthesis was found to be the best preferable technique whereas the physicochemical was found to be the least preferable method among the adjacent alternatives. Fuzzy PROMETHEE is highly sensitive and effective in the ranking process. It aids decision-makers and engineers in making good beneficial choices for both the industry and society.

articleTitle: Performance assessment of rooftop PV/T systems based on adaptive and smart cooling facility scheme - a case in hot climatic conditions of Sharjah, UAE
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Substantial interest in solar energy and its abundance has paved the way for the steady incorporation of smart schemes and sensor technologies to enhance the overall performance of Photovoltaic (PV) systems. A major dilemma represented by photovoltaic technologies is their electrical conversion rate which accounts for 20%, while the remainder is dissipated as waste heat that consequently affects the PV module's performance and leads to its degradation. Currently, the predicament of excessive heat on PV modules has been sought by the introduction of Photovoltaic/Thermal (PV/T) technologies, which proposes a methodology of harnessing both electric and thermal energies, hence improving the overall performance of the PV system. In this study, a real-time experimental investigation is conducted based on a proposed smart front-cooling methodology for a mounted rooftop PV/T system of 110 W capacity during the harsh summer climate in Sharjah, UAE. The primary emphasis of this investigation is to assess the deployment of an adaptive framework that detects a temperature limit of 55°C to facilitate the automated distribution of water on the fore face of the PV system using microcontroller and sensor technologies in real-time conditions. The proposed methodology enhanced the maximum DC power generated by 39.21%, reaching 40.21 W and 35.42 W with and without cooling, respectively. Moreover, an overall increment in electrical efficiency was observed up to 12.49% with the proposed cooling methodology as compared to 11.00% for the reference PV module. Furthermore, the proposed automated cooling methodology provided a thermal difference (ΔT) of 15.41°C, which represents the harnessed thermal energy that can be explicitly used for domestic/industrial preheating applications.

articleTitle: Authentication mechanisms used in Wireless Body Area Networks: a study
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: The WBANs (Collection of light-weight body sensor) of IOT and Cloud Computing provides a substantial ability to upgrade the quality of on-demand health care system. Body Sensors are implanted within or outside the human being body to remotely measure the real-time parameters such as physiology signal and activity. The biggest issue originates from obtaining imprecise and inconsistent measurements when collecting these data from sensor nodes. Moreover, Privacy and Security of human sensitive information are other biggest hurdles of WBANs. In this chapter we describe some wearable devices, security requirements and some security attacks. Moreover, we also discussed various existing authentication mechanisms. Different authentication mechanisms have their own Pros and Cons. Further, based on the study we will performed some comprehensive overview between all existing authentication mechanisms and find some future scope. We also highlight some future research scope in the last section.

articleTitle: Ensemble of 3D CNNs for brain MRI segmentation
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Generating pseudo computed tomography (CT) images from magnetic resonance images (MRI) is an essential task for a variety of medical imaging applications. This task is performed by segmenting the brain image into multiple tissue classes: bone, soft tissue, and air where bone segmentation is the most challenging part. The aim of this work is to propose an ensemble of excitation-based CNNs for enhancing the bone segmentation in brain T1-weighted MRI. In order to create diversity, multiple 3D excitation-based CNNs which employ different combinations of activation and loss functions are aggregated to build an ensemble model that provides reliable segmentation results. Using 3D clinical MR and CT images of fifty patients, the proposed approach is evaluated by performing a comparison between segmented MRI and segmented CT. This work is also validated with the baseline approach and other methods reported in the literature. The ensemble model with three CNNs shows superior segmentation results compared to a single CNN model by considering the three tissue classes where the DSC is improved from 0.618 to 0.657, from 0.907 to 0.914, and from 0.965 to 0.962 for bone, soft tissue, and air classes, respectively. The presented ensemble model reveals its potential to boost the segmentation results compared to the segmentation results obtained by a single CNN. v

articleTitle: 3D electrical impedance tomography system for real-time annular multiphase flow metering
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: With the rapid progress of tomography systems, a need has emerged for innovation that can provide high accuracy measurements, fast acquisition rate, and low-cost robust systems for multi-phase flow and medical instruments. The main objective of this work is to design and implement a 3D Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) system to effectively monitor a multi-phase flow which consists of an annular flow comprising of an air-core of unknown diameter, surrounded by a liquid phase, such as oil and water mixture of high water-cut value. The system consists of an array of electrode sensors evenly distributed around the pipe confining the three-phase flow. Subsequently, a dedicated hardware module (GPU) is used to reconstruct these signals, captured from the sensors, into a 3D image of the flow by solving the forward-inverse problem. The annular flow is generated using a flow conditioner consisting of a swirl cage followed by a bluff body that generates vortices that push the high dense liquid phase to the outer side of the pipeline. The 3D EIT system is designed to accurately measure the gas liquid fraction and the liquid-liquid fraction and provide the 3D volume image of the flow. Hence, it can be utilized for pipeline and reservoirs characterization to achieve high efficiency, cost reduction, and safer production. The approach is to design a dedicated, highly parallel hardware architecture that can sustain the high computation complexity of the 3D EIT algorithm. Coincidentally, advanced software development tools are available to help effectively develop these parallel hardware algorithms. The main novelty is utilizing GPUs to outperform the existing real-time tomography hardware platforms, mainly based on Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGAs), which have the disadvantage of being less dense and feature lower precise arithmetic operations. Matrix multiplication and matrix inversion are considered the most intensive computation in Electric Impedance Tomography (EIT). Therefore, GPU threads will be utilized for faster matrix multiplication/inversion in the proposed design, which is the pipeline for real-time reconstruction. Preliminary results were obtained by running matrix multiplication simulation for different sizes of matrices and comparing their computation time to validate that running matrix multiplication on the GPU threads is faster than sequentially executed on the CPU. For example, the multiplication done in parallel on the NVIDIA 2080 RTX GPU for a matrix of size 10000x10000 was 54.6% faster than sequentially on the Intel i7-9700k CPU. In conclusion, the innovation in this paper is achieving real-time image reconstruction for annular multi-phase flow by incorporating GPUs and open-source EIT toolkits to construct an effective, non-intrusive multi-phase flow measurement system (MPFM) based on electrical tomography.

articleTitle: TOPSIS multi-criteria decision-making method for mechanical energy storage systems' evaluation
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Electricity expenditure has been continuously increasing yearly. Hence, renewable energy sources have been proposed as viable alternatives to fossil fuels for clean energy supply. However, some of these renewable energy sources cannot operate independently. Hence, energy storage systems must be incorporated into the energy mix to guarantee uninterrupted supply. These storage systems are integral to the modern electrical grid to preclude issues induced by using renewable energy sources. Mechanical energy storage is a subcategory of energy storage technologies. It includes old technologies such as pumped hydro storage and more modern technologies such as flywheel and compressed air energy storage. This paper reports on employing the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) to compare and rank these storage systems based on operational parameters. Given its response time, the flywheel storage system is the top-ranked mechanical system based on the specific parameters defined in this paper. After the ranking procedure, this paper offers a future outlook of these storage systems and the direction they are heading towards. It is noted that the future digitalization and industrialization tendencies require the exploration of the status of the energy storage sector in this regard.

articleTitle: Intelligent PSO approach for QoS-aware web service selection
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Various providers can supply the various services, in a service-oriented setting, each with its own unique set of non-functional Quality of Service (QoS) qualities. Web service selection efficiency will always decay as the number of offered services grows because many already-existing services share identical QoS characteristics. There must be a method for choosing which individual services will go into other related fields so that it may fulfill its consumers' expectations for quality of service. Many services exist with the same QoS and provide the same functionality therefore choosing the best services from many candidates is a research issue. When selecting services of good quality and with less computation time, it will affect the efficiency of the next operations such as service composition and service recommendation. In this paper, a new improved Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is proposed to solve the mentioned issue of service selection. To find the global optimal solution for selecting dynamic web services while maintaining the quality of service, this study introduces a new single parameter and evolution-based enhancement system to improve PSO-based web service selection (IPSO-SS). The IPSO tries to avoid the local optimum to find the global solution for the problem of service composition. IPSO-SS is practical and effective in the service selection process, as evidenced by theoretical experimental and analysis findings. The experiments conducted on QWS datasets showed that the proposed approach IPSO-SS outperformed other approaches in terms of computation time and convergence rate.

articleTitle: Detection of Alzheimer's disease using machine learning models: the impact of pre-processing
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a brain ailment that causes memory loss, disorientation, personality changes, and a loss of independence over time. People with this disease initially experience minor memory loss and confusion. This is referred to as cognitive deterioration. However, as time passes, these symptoms get more acute. On the other hand, as there is no cure for this disease, medical professionals concentrate on detecting dementia in its early stages, this helps them determine the best treatments and allows patients to take precautionary measures before any damage happens to their brain which is irreversible. As a result, researchers focus on using machine learning models that can give significant results in identifying symptoms of dementia in the early stages. In this paper, we employed machine learning methods to identify the various phases of dementia using brain MRI scans. We used multiple traditional algorithms such as XGBoost, AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, Decision trees, SVM, Logistic regression, Random forest, and KNearest Neighbor. We compared the performance of these algorithms with and without the use of preprocessing techniques. Our best model was the SVM model with an accuracy of 100% after applying preprocessing. In addition, we used a transfer learning model that achieves an accuracy of 90%. Thus, our work demonstrated the effect of preprocessing on enhancing the results of the traditional algorithms and transfer learning models in identifying the stages of dementia.

articleTitle: An extensible framework for curricula forecasting in software engineering programs
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Universities have the responsibility to ensure that their courses prepare students with skills relevant to their future careers. As observed in many specific domains, there is often a gap between university curricula and industry needs. Such a gap is always attributed to both the remain of outdated materials and the oversight of new and relevant topics promptly due to the unavailability of a solution to keep curricula in synchronization with the continuous changes in the industry. This issue is, however, most prominent in technology-dependent disciplines, such as software engineering, where techniques, approaches, environments, and tools change continuously. While it is true that software engineering graduates will have to continuously update their knowledge during their careers, filling the skillset gap between their knowledge and the future employer's needs at the beginning of a career could be overwhelming. The aforementioned issue is a well-known problem and some common practices have been in place to resolve this issue such as bi-yearly meetings with industry board members, yearly course assessments, and individual efforts to update the course material. However, none of these provide a dynamic solution to align software engineering curricula and industry needs, maintaining such an alignment, and prompt in-time changes, as the current mechanism, often depend on the expertise and the progressive thinking of faculty. To fill this gap, this work proposes an extensible framework to proactively work in tandem with a software engineering program, serving as a “curricula forecasting” tool to support both change control and new topics/courses recommendations with longer-term visions.

articleTitle: Forecasting Dubai City water demand using the fuzzy logic approach
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: The United Arab Emirates is one of the largest global consumers of desalinated water. Therefore, it is imperative to properly manage current water sources while planning for future demand and operation. One important management tool is to forecast future demand from past and present water demand. One potential prediction tool is the fuzzy logic method that can be used to model nonlinear data. One of the main advantages of the fuzzy logic method is that it does not carry many assumptions, ergodicity and stationarity of other statistical techniques. This research utilises the Mamdani approach to predict the water demand from three antecedent water consumption values, with the model analysed using the MATLAB software for four different membership functions, namely Triangular, Trapezoidal, Gaussian and the Generalised bell-shaped membership function. The analysis highlighted that the triangular, trapezoidal and generalised bell-shaped membership functions indicated a minimum error, with the Gaussian membership function demonstrating results removed from the other three membership functions. The research concludes that utilising hybrid models, improving the quality of data and utilising a robust set of rules can improve the model's performance in predicting water consumption.

articleTitle: The impact of feature quality on SDN traffic learning and classification
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Network traffic classification is crucial for facilitating sophisticated network management. Software-defined networks (SDN) provide a featured architecture where the control and data planes are decoupled to enable dynamic configuration. The control plane functionality is implemented in a programmable centralized controller that enables effective use of data-driven based on network traffic classification using efficient machine learning (ML) algorithms. However, there is a lack of standardized benchmarking criteria agreed by the SDN community to evaluate the techniques proposed to collect and classify the network traffic features. This paper presents an empirical analysis to investigate the impact of SDN traffic features on the performance of ML-based classifiers. This study has been conducted using a publicly available SDN traffic dataset. The procedure of feature engineering has also been comprehensively evaluated through three approaches of feature selection, which are low variance filter, high correlation filter, and backward feature elimination. The experimental results show that the performance of ML classifiers is highly driven by the quality traffic features fed to them; the highest quality the traffic features are the best accuracy is achieved.

articleTitle: Security in Robot Operating Systems (ROS): analytical review study
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: The Robotic Operating System (ROS) is a popular framework for robotics research and development. It's a system that provides hardware abstraction with low-level device management to handle communications and services. ROS is a distributed system, which allows various nodes in a network to communicate using a method such as message passing. When integrating systems using ROS, it is vital to consider the security and privacy of the data and information shared across ROS nodes, which is considered to be one of the most challenging aspects of ROS systems. The goal of this study is to examine the ROS architecture, primary components, and versions, as well as the types of vulnerabilities that might compromise the system. In order to achieve the CIA's three fundamental security criteria on a ROS-based platform, we categorized these vulnerabilities and looked into various security solutions proposed by researchers. We provide a comparative analysis of the ROS-related security solutions, the security threats and issues they addressed, the targeted architecture of the protection or defense system, the solution's evaluation methodology and the evaluation metric, and the limitations that might be viewed as unresolved issues for the future course of action. Finally, we look into future possibilities and open challenges to assist researchers to develop more secure and efficient ROS systems.

articleTitle: Prototyping an environmental sensor network for meteorological and climate studies at the city scale
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Understanding and managing climate change at the city scale requires collecting environmental data with a temporal and spatial resolution that is not typically available to research institution. As a contribution towards filling this gap, we present the general architecture of an internet-of-things (IoT) sensor network for environmental research at the city scale. We describe in detail the software and hardware design of the IoT measurement devices, which are built from inexpensive, off-the-shelf sensors and components. A prototype version of the network is currently under test at the New York University Abu Dhabi campus. We show some encouraging preliminary data and discuss future enhancements.

articleTitle: A decision-making model for treatment alternatives of different clinical abdominal aortic aneurysm presentations
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm (AAA) is the dilatation of the abdominal aorta for a diameter larger than 3 centimeters. The worst clinical scenario for a surgeon is a patient with ruptured AAA. Therefore, treatment is essential for patients with abdominal aorta's measuring larger than diameter of 5.5 centimeters in the infrarenal region. Treatment methods available are open surgery and endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Both techniques have many advantages and disadvantages, which makes decision-making a very complex process for the surgeon, especially if a rupture exists. Even though only two treatment options are available for the surgical treatment of AAA, it is essential and not easy to determine the best option for a specific patient. This study aims to evaluate EVAR and open surgery technique by using the fuzzy preference ranking organization method for enrichment evaluation (PROMETHEE), which is an analytical multi-criteria decision-making model, in scenarios of non-chronic and non-ruptured (stable), chronic, and ruptured AAA patients. The current study is the first study in the literature which contains different scenarios supports the decision for the AAA patients treatment options with the mathematical modelling by considering numerous number of the criteria simultaneouslly. In this study, the selected criteria of the AAA treatment parameters are hospitalization duration, cost of treatments, ICU stay duration, anesthesia depth, intubation duration, postoperative rehabilitation duration, postoperative follow-up frequency, radiation-based follow-up investigations, operation risk, disease-free follow-up duration, additional procedure requirement, multidisciplinary approach requirement, perioperative risk, perioperative blood transfusion requirement, perioperative radiation exposure, surgery duration, postoperative respiratory complications, mortality risk, and 5-year prognosis. With fuzzy logic, values of the parameters of the AAA treatments are determined as a fuzzy number assigned to linguistic expressions; then, using the PROMETHEE method, which is based on the pairwise comparison technique, the best alternative treatment option of the AAA has been computed for different conditions of the patients considering the importance weights assigned to each criterion based on the expert's opinions and experiences. The result suggests that EVAR would be the preferred treatment choice for chronic AAA patients with 0,0012 net outranking value and ruptured AAA patients with 0,0017 net outranking value. In contrast, open surgery would be a superior choice for stable patients with 0,0027 net outranking value. The results may change based on the preferences of the decision maker while computing the weights of the parameters/criteria and also as a result of technological developments in cardiovascular surgery field in the future.

articleTitle: Brain sight: a novel system for substituting vision sensor
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: In a world where nearly everything we do depends on sight; it is ever more challenging for the unsighted to cope with it and lead a normal life without being reliant on the presence of a companion. Finding a mechanism to convey visual information to the brain is the most difficult part of the research as well as the development of efficient sensory replacement and augmentation systems. In this paper, we aim to propose Brain Sight as an innovative system to help blind people identifying and discovering things in front of them using vibro-tactile display for vision sensory substitution. Brain Sight is a wearable vest-like fabric containing small vibration motors that displays pulses to map the seen images on the Lower-back of the visually impaired. A deep labeling segmentation and edge detection techniques are applied to the captured image after preprocessing. A simple prototype is implemented and tested with volunteers. Thanks to neuroplasticity and the cognitive cortex inside humans' brain, the implemented vest showed promising results. Without the need for intensive training, Brain Sight enables blind to recognize different shapes and numbers.

articleTitle: Speech emotion recognition framework and applications in emergency call centers
publicationTitle: The 3rd International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2022)
abstract: Nowadays, Emotion recognition using speech signals plays a significant role in various applications including lie detection, security issues, and emergency call centers. Speech emotion recognition can be used to detect such as fear, sadness, and happiness that could help in making effective decisions. Speech emotion recognition is used to extract emotions from speech signals. Our proposed system has three main stages which are feature extraction, Feature selection, and classifications. The main goal of this work is to design a framework for call center applications using speech emotion recognition. The framework will start with preprocessing step in which noise will be removed from the input speech signal using filters. Next, we applied Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) algorithms to extract the features. In the third stage Support Vector Machine classifier is utilized to identify the emotional state that was extracted from our proposed features.
